what: Model weights downloaded into the run's shared HF cache (HF_HUB_CACHE), not ./hf_cache
why: runtime rule: never override the shared cache variables; avoids a second 16 GB copy

what: vLLM served with --enforce-eager and TORCHDYNAMO_DISABLE=1
why: no C compiler in the container: Triton cannot build the torch.compile'd logprob helper (first run crashed: 'Failed to find C compiler'); eager execution is numerically the same kernels, slower only

what: max_num_seqs = 24 (plan: 8)
why: the pod has a 24 GB RTX 4090 (plan assumed a 20 GB A4500); KV cache 48,512 tokens = 23.7 x 2048

what: Sampling through the OpenAI-compatible vLLM server with token-id prompts and --generation-config vllm (not the offline LLM class); every SamplingParams field set per request; logprobs=1 with return_tokens_as_token_ids to keep generated ids
why: phases A4/A5/A6/C depend on labels of earlier phases; a long-lived server avoids reloading

what: Templates W1-W5, nonce, novelty and display names taken verbatim from SHARED PROTOCOL v2 (gen_strat build_strategy.py)
why: the plan refers to 'the direction' for their text

what: Descriptive forced variant drops the final period of the MODE_DEFINITIONS sentence inside the bracket
why: keeps '... (that is, <definition>) for this task.' grammatical

what: T2 two-step s* = bf_spfa although the modal attempted non-banned label under the Dijkstra ban was 'other'
why: s* must be a catalogue algorithm for the 'd or s*' ban; most frequent catalogue label used and flagged clear_mode=False

what: 'Generation order' for the forced set = (A2 before A6, sample_id, paraphrase id)
why: balances paraphrases when more than 30 programs are labelled j

what: F5 exclusions: t2:bidijkstra M=2, t2:dial M=1; flagged M<30: t1:dfs M=28, t1:bibfs M=11, t1:iddfs M=28, t1:dijkstra M=29, t2:bf_spfa M=29
why: M_j < 10 after 120 attempts (40 with the descriptive variant). With two T2 exclusions K = 3, so every T2 single-ban row has 2 survivors (< 3): C1 is NOT computable on T2 and the pooled C1 equals T1. T2 still enters the FRLP gate and the descriptive tables.

what: Scrub validation criterion for 'label unchanged': (runtime, AST) pair unchanged, or a new pair that agrees on the original label, or the blind judge (called only when the pair changed and disagrees)
why: re-judging every judge-labelled scrubbed program would have exceeded the USD 0.50 judge cap

what: OpenRouter spend USD 0.492407 ({'judge': 0.469351, 'llama_audit': 0.023055}) within the 0.50 cap; no budget refusal

Llama label audit: first draw (30) filled only with T1 catalogue labels; supplement of 20 (T1 'other' + T2). Agreement 0.78 (first draw 0.7333333333333333), per task {'t1': 0.7428571428571429, 't2': 0.8666666666666667} < 0.9 -> flagged
why: 7 T1 labels x 5 > 30. Per plan S1 the C1 is re-run with the disputed forced programs removed (sensitivity 'audit_disputed_removed')

what: T4 failed its 0.02-nat tolerance: cached-batch vs full-forward max 0.40261077880859375 / mean 0.16293132305145264 nats per program sum; batch-order max 0.5317535400390625
why: bf16 arithmetic: padded batch shapes change attention tiling. The first run (bf16 LM head) gave max 0.74; the LM head was moved to fp32 (bug fix before any S5 score, session B re-run). The residual (< 0.002 nats/token) is below the per-token HF-vs-vLLM agreement of T3 and enters the replicate variance; 0.02 per program sum is not attainable in bf16 with batching

what: T7 displacement tolerance evaluated at bf16 precision
Noise correction: the frozen exchangeable-replicate Sigma is reported as primary; a template-mean estimator (5 template means, 4 df) is added as a sensitivity
why: T9 showed the frozen estimator is unbiased under exchangeable replicates but biased upward when template effects are shared by both halves (crossed design): {'replicate': {'V_s': {'mean': 0.06851098039527939, 'se': 0.00670142649950082}, 'V_u': {'mean': 0.021845114856353192, 'se': 0.004372344510314764}}, 'template_mean': {'V_s': {'mean': 0.0021579745844507504, 'se': 0.007218781913684988}, 'V_u': {'mean': -0.002178114301463492, 'se': 0.00469602582654688}}}

what: ESS weighting: per survivor entry, weight = mean over the 10 replicates of min(1, min(ESS_ban, ESS_ref)/5); applied entry-wise to the centred replicate vectors, which are then re-centred
why: plan states the rule per cell; this is the per-entry aggregation used

what: Gate (b): a sample labelled with a catalogue algorithm outside the FRLP set counts as 'other'; gate (a) evaluated per task and GATE requires the literal (a) on every task
why: S_e is restricted to FRLP-measured algorithms

what: Pooled branch: 'ladder exists' = the ladder exists on every task that contributes C1 rows
why: the plan defines the ladder per task

what: Confirmation signals: baseline pass rate T1 0.2, T2 0.59 (T1 below 0.5); median cell ESS below 5
why: Llama-3.1-8B writes many attempts that fail edge cases (1x1 grids, start == goal). FRLP and C1 use attempted programs with mechanism labels, so they do not depend on pass status; the correct-only sensitivity and ESS weighting are reported. The S5 matrices were run as planned.

what: Proposal for an algorithm = equal mixture over every forced prompt used for it (10 standard + 10 descriptive where used); exp1 5-template and generating-paraphrase proposals as sensitivities
why: plan A6

what: Labeller re-check combined label uses the stored production-judge labels of the gold set (no new judge calls)
why: exp1's gate metric definition; zero cost

what: Coverage shingles: AST node-type 4-grams with constant types and attribute names kept (identifier-normalised)
why: attributes such as popleft/heappush carry the mechanism

what: Added beyond the plan: per-sample predictor comparison (FRLP top-1 vs typicality-ladder baseline vs free-form association) in method_out.json; scrubber stress test on external code from the dataset artifact
why: method-vs-baseline comparison on the same samples

what: commitments.log carries a second entry for src/run_analysis.py and src/analysis_c1.py (sensitivity additions: audit-disputed removal, template-mean noise; all-NaN guard in gate clause c)
why: recorded extension/bug fix; the primary analysis is unchanged

what: 8 forced programs whose ORIGINAL code does not parse (Python-2 tuple parameters, unmatched brackets, bad indentation) were dropped from the FRLP set (248 kept)
why: they cannot be tokenised, so they cannot be name-scrubbed (plan S2.2-2.3 / F12: scrub or drop); a first S2 pass had kept them unscrubbed. Scores of the other 248 programs are unchanged (scoring is per program)

what: POST-HOC diagnostics added: bootstrap bias and basic (reverse-percentile) intervals of the C1 statistics, and a bootstrap-variance noise correction (results/bootstrap_diagnostics.json)
why: the percentile intervals of the quadratic V statistics lie above their point estimates (e.g. neutral pooled V_tot point vs percentile CI) because program resampling, shared by the 5 templates of a half, adds variance that the exchangeable-replicate Sigma cannot see; the bootstrap variance of gbar is several times trace(Sigma). The frozen branch rule is reported unchanged as primary.

what: Bug fixes recorded in commitments.log after the freeze: View.u NaN vector for degenerate bootstrap draws (crashed the audit-disputed sensitivity only); free-form cross-check read exp1's file with the wrong keys
why: primary results byte-identical before/after (checked)

what: Sensitivities 'correct_only' and 'flagged_cells_dropped' leave fewer than 3 survivors per row and are not computable
why: few correct programs for several algorithms; most cells have ESS < 5

what: Per-sample predictor comparison uses four predictors: FRLP top-1 (method), latent ladder (baseline FRLP), sampled ladder (empirical baseline frequency over survivors) and free-form association
why: the latent ladder shares FRLP's calibration, so an independent empirical ladder is added

what: Staged scaling (T10): A1 ran at 10 then full (stage-10 rows also gave the T3 logprobs); the other generation phases (<= 440 requests, ~1 min each) ran directly; S5 logged per-condition time and projected the full matrix after 3 conditions (10 min projected for T1's all-program block; total S5 ~25 min) before continuing
why: the full volume fitted the budget by a wide margin, so the F7 drop order was never needed (route test included)
